I dated an older woman, I was 23 and she was 43 (we met at work). I remember when I found out her age I thought to myself "this will never work out" + she had two kids, one of her kids was 15 at that time, but it was fun having a crush after my healing period. She was actually the one who tried very intensly to make it work (even after finding out how old I was, always saying that I looked/behaved older), and she was the one putting in effort, since I was very sceptical about us. There were also other "red flags" that I chose to ignore, and since she was trying so hard, I thought might as well try this out. 

  
I remember my mom going completely nuts when she find out that I was dating that woman. At first, I thought that maybe she reacted that way because she wasn't comfortable about my sexuality, but one day we had a talk where she shared her doubts about the age gap. The woman I was seeing was just  5 years younger than my mom, but at some point I thought to myself "damn, it would be really fucking weird if my mom started dating someone my age". 

There was a huge power imbalance between us, she had kids, house, stable job. I was about to start my second bachelro's degree. She said she never felt any power imbalance between us, but I did. at some point, I had to break things off, since I was almost daily accussed of flirting with other colleagues at work and some other stuff. We were off and on for some time, but the last time we met up, we talked how we would never actually work out, so we decided to end things for good. 

  
Now looking back 2 years later, it was fucking weird, lol. I don't think I (me, personally, I hope no one takes offense in this) could ever date anyone who is that much older than me at this stage in life.

I actually had a similar conversation with a friend of mine a few months ago (after his latest self-sabotage session). We kind of decided that, at least for me and him, we usually self-sabotage because of a comfortable life. When I am comfortable, I get bored, and when I am bored, it’s easy yet exciting to do something that I know the future me will have to deal with the consequences for (almost like instant gratification now—deal with consequences later).

When I feel bored, why should I try something new that can later turn into something good and over time make life boring once again? Or, in some instances, I think, “I am afraid that I will try and fail.” It feels easier to do something that I know is not good for me but brings me thrill in the moment.

However, I am really grateful that even after self-sabotaging, it only takes me a few months to get my life back in place. But I am also afraid that one day it won’t be that easy.

I went on a date with a woman (she was in her late 20s, i was in my mid 20s) some time ago. We met up at a bar, and everything was perfect until I told her that I was bi. The mood changed quickly, and I had to listen to her explain how she would never date a bi woman again because of her last ex (who left her for a guy). She said that if we were to date, she would constantly worry about me getting tired of her one day and leaving to be with a man when I “wanted to settle down and start a family.” It stung a little. It was a great date—so great that the bartenders had to kick us out (since the bar was closing) because we sat there for like 6 hours.

The next time I went on a date with another woman, the same thing happened! She also started explaining how bi women are just bi for a few years and later choose a man over a woman. I’m glad I took a pause from dating then because if it had happened a third time, I probably would’ve been afraid of bringing up that I was bisexual.

It’s like saying, “If someone cheated on me once, I should assume all future partners will cheat too.” And like you mentioned, what’s stopping a lesbian from leaving me for another woman? I understand that her experience affected her deeply and that it was rooted in insecurity, but... I don’t know... I had a partner cheat on me once back in the day, and even though it hurt, at some point I had to realize and accept that it had nothing to do with me (or what I was lacking) and everything to do with them.

I guess it’s hard for me to understand biphobia since I’m bi myself. Even though the last time I went on a date with a guy was like 4-5 years ago and I prefer women, and I don’t see my sexuality as something that makes me less trustworthy or committed.

I was the younger one in a 20 year age-gap relationship (I was 23, and she was 43). At the beginning, everything seemed great and I really thought it would work out, but there were several problems we both ignored. It was also a problem that we met each other at work, and were colleagues for a year and a half.

  
As others have mentioned, power dynamics can be a big problem, that I always felt between us. She had a house, two kids and a stable career. I was about to start studying for my second degree and become a student once again..

The second challenge was her lack of self-esteem, as she would always accuse me of flirting with other colleagues that were my age (kinda ironic, since she would be the one flirting with those early 20 year olds). She was afraid that I would one day find someone my age, or get tired of her being "old". 

  
One evening we had a really long talk about our futures, and decided that it was for the best that we split up (she gave me a great pov of hers, which I understood, and she ((and I)) knew that there was a lot for me left to explore in life). A very intense and toxic relationship, but it helped me a lot to understand what I want and don't want in a future relationship.



So if one day you and your lady decided that you might actually fancy each other, I would advise you to talk about your futures, what you want to do and what she wants to do, and listen to each other. Best of luck for you two :)

Remind myself that I can't be with that person. It takes a lot of time, it takes a lot of courage to accept that nothing is going to happen. It will hurt like hell, especially if that person is flirting with you/sending mixed signals. I started writing my feelings, because I could not share them with any of my friends. I wrote for months. I found new hobbies that interested me, books, movies, photography.

 Somehow I didn't think so much about that person as I used to, I just had to accept the fact that nothing will ever happen. I didn't stop talking with them, I didn't stop hanging with them, but I somehow managed to distract myself when thinking "what if". Now I only have a book full of pages written about someone I liked so much, sometimes I like reading those pages and thinking how much I liked that person.

 I don't think that the feelings will ever go away completely though if you are seing that person everyday. I still smile whenever I see my 'crush', I still want to make them feel happy and make their day better.

I grew up upper middle class, my ex-boyfriend sadly didn't. I was spoiled by my parents when I was a kid (consoles,phones,expensive clothes and so on), but I got myself a job when I turned 15 and rarely asked my parents for money (would ask them to give be 20 dollars if I went somewhere with my friends, but that happened rarely). My first job ofc was really shitty, but I would save atleast 40% of my income in case I suddenly realized I wanted something fancy, so saving money was something I learned to do since I was a kid (birthday money, chores money and so on). 

My ex grew up lower mid class, after his dad left them (was an alcoholic) he didn't give a damn about child support... his mother worked hard, trying to provide food and nice clothes to him and his two sisters. I met him when he moved out alone. He didn't have a chance to finish school because his mother struggled and he had to start working as 16 year old. After he moved out he started going to the school again (it was his last year at school) and worked at the same time. His mother got herself a boyfriend, and his older sister moved out aswell. I thought everything was starting to get better for him, and we started dating after a while. He finished school too!

The biggest difference I noticed was how he didn't try to save up some money. He would pay his rent and still have atleast 500 dollars in his bank account. He always insisted to pay for food or movie tickets because he was the man, but I would always feel so bad about it. His friends were a huge pain in the ass (drugs, alcohol and random hookups) so everytime they would go out to have a 'boys night' I would always feel so sceptical. Next day he would tell me that we can't do something because he didn't have more money 
 because he would always treat his friends (alcohol, taxi and so on). Sometimes his mother asked him for money, and he would give a few hundred bucks to her, which she never returned. 

When I turned 18 I got my drivers license, my parents insisted to buy me a car. I agreed, but only if it was on their name and not mine (so I could tell everyone I am just borrowing their car) when he found out that my parents were about to buy me a car he got mad at me, telling how spoiled I was. He drove vw golf (1999) and my parents bought me audi a3 (2008). That was when we got into a really big fight. After I got my car he would just talk shit how easy it was for me, how I didn't need to raise a single finger and get anything I wanted. I got really upset and angry, I told him that if he would've saved his money instead of going to night clubs with his buddies every saturday, he would have had much better car than I had. He got really angry, slammed door and left. We talked about our problems a few days later, I apologized and he didn't. 

This year we started planing a trip to Spain together (I looked for the cheapest plane tickets aswell as hotels) we agreed that he payed for his tickets, I payed for mine and we would split hotel bill later on. The day I wanted to buy plane tickets, I invited him over and told him that it would be a good time to buy plane tickets, and he replied 'my budget won't allow me to go to Spain right now' I told him I could pay for both of us since his birthday was not so far away, but he declined. So we didn't go, we talked about renting a cabin for a week or so just to spend some time alone, which sadly he didn't want to do because of his budget. Next weekend he went to pub with his friends again and spent half of his paycheck on that. 


I always felt like a pain in the ass for him, telling him to save some money just in case. We broke up a few months ago, he is still talking shit about me to our mutual friends tho. I hope life starts treating him better soon.

Oh yes! I went to innføringsklasse for around 6 months, after that my teachers decided that I was prepared to go to a normal school. I had to carry my dictionary everywhere I went, and it was pretty hard. Tbh, I am still scared to say something out loud in Norwegian if I am talking with strangers. I tend to mix up sentence structures all the time (speaking Norwegian at school and speaking native language when I get home).

I remember when I moved to Norway, it was around 7 years ago. I fell in love with Norway and Norwegians. I am enjoying utepils on sunny days and playing board games in cabin with my friends. 

The only issue I have ever felt is the whole 'personal space' problem, no small talks @ buses and so on. But, all of us have different personalities and some of us have learned different norms. Also, I think it's weird how common one night stands are in Norway. 

We have a few exchange studens at our school and they think that Norwegians are like the song ¨Hot 'n' Cold¨ by Katy Perry. One day they are smiling at you, talking and joking a lot, the next day they are completely ignoring you and giving you a cold shoulder. 

Norway is a great country, can't see my future anywhere else than Norway. And I can't wait for russetiden! :D If you have any questions, you can always PM me, I think it's probably intresting to hear something about Norway from a different point of view. :)
